Hainan Country Garden Real Estate Development Co., Ltd. v. Sanya Kaili Investment Co., Ltd., Zhang Weinan, et al. — dispute over confirmation of contract validity

【Ruling Summary】

Where a company's shareholder only engages in a single act of transferring corporate funds, which is insufficient to deny the separate legal personality of the company, the shareholder shall not be held jointly and severally liable for the company's debts under Article 20, Paragraph 3 of the Company Law. However, such act objectively transfers and reduces the company's assets, thereby diminishing the company's debt-servicing capacity. In accordance with the principle of "a fortiori" (referring to the heavier as a guide for the lighter), and with reference to Article 14 of the Provisions of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues concerning the Application of the Company Law of the People's Republic of China (III), which governs the liability form in cases of capital contribution withdrawal by shareholders, the court may rule that the shareholder shall bear supplementary compensation liability for the portion of the company's debts that cannot be satisfied, within the amount of the transferred funds and the corresponding interest.

Civil Judgment of the Supreme People's Court
(2019) Supreme People's Court Final Civil No. 960

Appellants (Defendants at First Instance): Sanya Kaili Investment Co., Ltd., domiciled at Room 703, Building B, Chuangye Mansion, Xinfeng Road, Tianya District, Sanya City, Hainan Province.
Legal Representative: Liang Lu, General Manager of the company.

Appellant (Defendant at First Instance): Zhang Weinan, male, born on February 26, 1968, Han ethnicity, domiciled in Haikou City, Hainan Province.

Jointly authorized agent ad litem for the above two appellants: Lin Jiancai, lawyer of Hainan Waijing Law Firm.

Respondent (Plaintiff at First Instance): Hainan Country Garden Real Estate Development Co., Ltd., domiciled at Floor A-12, Hainan Binhai International Financial Center, No. 117 Binhai Avenue, Longhua District, Haikou City, Hainan Province.
Legal Representative: Ye Jianqing.
Authorized agent ad litem: Dong Jicheng, male, employee of the company.
Authorized agent ad litem: Hong Haowei, male, employee of the company.

Defendant at First Instance: Liang Lu, female, born on May 4, 1978, Han ethnicity, domiciled in Dongcheng District, Beijing City.

Defendant at First Instance: Tibet Shengfang Investment Co., Ltd., domiciled at Room 2-2, Unit 3, Building 4, Area A, Sunshine New Town, No. 158 Jinzhu West Road, Lhasa Economic and Technological Development Zone, Tibet Autonomous Region.
Legal Representative: Wang Mingqiang, Executive Director and Manager of the company.

Third Party at First Instance: China Construction Bank Corporation, Sanya Branch, domiciled at No. 100 Commercial Street, Jiyang District, Sanya City, Hainan Province.
Person in Charge: Yang Jianhua, Branch Manager.
Authorized agent ad litem: Wang Jianhu, male, employee of the Branch.

In the case of dispute over confirmation of contract validity, the appellants Sanya Kaili Investment Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Kaili Company) and Zhang Weinan, in relation to the respondent Hainan Country Garden Real Estate Development Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Country Garden Company), the defendants at first instance Liang Lu and Tibet Shengfang Investment Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Shengfang Company), and the third party at first instance China Construction Bank Corporation, Sanya Branch (hereinafter referred to as CCB Sanya Branch), appealed against the civil judgment of the Hainan High People's Court (2018) Qiong Initial Civil No. 6. This Court, after accepting the case on June 13, 2019, formed a collegiate panel according to law and held a hearing. Lin Jiancai, the authorized agent ad litem of the appellants Kaili Company and Zhang Weinan, Dong Jicheng and Hong Haowei, the authorized agents ad litem of the respondent Country Garden Company, and Wang Jianhu, the authorized agent ad litem of the third party at first instance CCB Sanya Branch, appeared before the court to participate in the proceedings. The defendants at first instance Liang Lu and Shengfang Company, having been duly summoned by this Court, did not appear. This case is now concluded.

Kaili Company and Zhang Weinan appealed, requesting: (1) Revoke the first-instance judgment; (2) Amend to dismiss all of Country Garden Company's claims for rescission of the "Sanya Blue Moon Bay Seaview Hotel Apartment Project Asset Transfer Contract" (hereinafter referred to as the "Asset Transfer Contract"), for Kaili Company to refund the earnest money of RMB 320,000,000 and pay liquidated damages, and for priority compensation from the proceeds of the discounted or auctioned/sold land use rights and above-ground attachments owned by Kaili Company located on the east side of Hongsha Wangzhi Village, Jiyang District, Sanya City; (3) Amend to dismiss Country Garden Company's claim that Zhang Weinan bear joint and several liability for the debt owed by Kaili Company under the fourth adjudicative holding of the first-instance judgment; (4) Order Country Garden Company to bear all litigation costs for the first and second instances. The facts and reasons are as follows: (1) The first-instance judgment's findings regarding the validity of the "Asset Transfer Contract" and the "Entrusted Loan Contract," force majeure, rescission of the "Asset Transfer Contract," liquidated damages, and Country Garden Company's priority right to compensation over the land use rights and above-ground attachments in Kaili Company's name were unclear in fact and insufficient in evidence. (1) The first-instance judgment's conclusion that the "Asset Transfer Contract" and the "Entrusted Loan Contract" were valid was erroneous. These two contracts are of different natures and cannot both be found valid simultaneously. The "Entrusted Loan Contract" reflected the true intention of the parties, whereas the "Asset Transfer Contract," in name an asset transfer but in substance an entrusted loan, violates mandatory provisions of laws and administrative regulations and is therefore invalid. (2) Kaili Company's inability to perform was caused by government policy adjustments, which constitute force majeure. The "Asset Transfer Contract" was signed on July 15, 2017. In September of the same year, the Hainan Provincial People's Government issued a "two suspensions" policy, and in October, the project in question was suspended due to this policy. Government policy adjustments constitute force majeure, and Kaili Company should not be found in breach. (3) The first-instance judgment's conclusion that the "Asset Transfer Contract" was rescinded on November 12, 2017, was erroneous. The final performance deadline for the conditions precedent under the "Asset Transfer Contract" was October 30, 2017. Country Garden Company issued a "Refund Letter" on October 26, 2017, which was invalid. Consequently, the "Demand Letter" dated November 12, 2017, extending from that letter, is also invalid and cannot serve as a basis for rescission. (4) The first-instance judgment's calculation of liquidated damages at an annual rate of 24% was erroneous. First, the "Asset Transfer Contract" is invalid, and therefore Article 17's liquidated damages clause is also invalid. Second, the "Entrusted Loan Contract" stipulated an annual interest rate of 7%; the first-instance judgment's support for a 24% annual rate on the ground that borrowing costs or lending returns in real economic activities exceed that rate was improper. Third, Country Garden Company failed to prove it sustained any losses. (5) The first-instance judgment's finding that Country Garden Company had a priority right to compensation over the land use rights and above-ground attachments under certificate Qiong (2016) Sanya City Real Property No. XXXXXXXX in Kaili Company's name was erroneous. According to the "Mortgage Contract," the mortgagee was CCB Sanya Branch, not Country Garden Company. (2) The first-instance judgment's order that Zhang Weinan bear joint and several liability for Kaili Company's debt was erroneous. Kaili Company's transfer of RMB 29,518,384 to Zhang Weinan after receiving RMB 320,000,000 was a repayment of a loan, consistent with the use of loan funds stated in Article 2 of the "Entrusted Loan Contract," which includes repayment of shareholder loans and daily operational turnover. Zhang Weinan did not fabricate the RMB 20,000,000 loan; there was no disclosure of false information or false capital contribution, and no abuse of corporate independence or shareholder limited liability to evade debts, nor any serious harm to the interests of corporate creditors. (3) The first-instance judgment incorrectly applied the law. (1) Applying Articles 93 and 96 of the Contract Law of the PRC (hereinafter referred to as the "Contract Law") to find that the "Asset Transfer Contract" was rescinded on November 12, 2017, was an error in application of law. (2) Applying Article 26, Paragraph 1 of the Provisions of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues concerning the Application of Law in the Trial of Private Lending Cases to determine interest was an error in application of law. (3) Applying Article 20, Paragraph 3 of the Company Law of the PRC (hereinafter referred to as the "Company Law") to find that Zhang Weinan abused corporate independence and shareholder limited liability to evade debts was an error in application of law. (4) The substance of this case is a loan relationship; applying Articles 396 and 402 of the Contract Law in the first-instance judgment was erroneous. (5) The first-instance judgment found the "Asset Transfer Contract" valid, thereby rendering the conflicting "Entrusted Loan Contract" invalid, and consequently its accessory "Mortgage Contract" should also be invalid. The first-instance judgment, while still applying Articles 173 and 179 of the Property Law of the PRC (hereinafter referred to as the "Property Law") to find Country Garden Company entitled to priority compensation over the land use rights and above-ground attachments under certificate Qiong (2016) Sanya City Real Property No. XXXXXXXX, was erroneous. (4) Zhang Weinan, Liang Lu, and Shengfang Company were not proper defendants in this case; the first-instance court's inclusion of these three as defendants violated procedural law. (1) Zhang Weinan is a shareholder of Kaili Company, not a party to the "Asset Transfer Contract." Under the principle of privity of contract, Country Garden Company cannot assert claims against Zhang Weinan. (2) Country Garden Company's claim that Zhang Weinan and Shengfang Company fabricated debts and transferred corporate assets to harm its interests constitutes a tort action, whereas this case is an action to confirm contract validity. The shareholder tort action should be heard separately. (3) A shareholder tort action is not a necessary joint action; the first-instance court should not have included Zhang Weinan, Liang Lu, and Shengfang Company as defendants.

Country Garden Company argued: (1) The "Entrusted Loan Contract" and the "Asset Transfer Contract" are inseparable; the "Entrusted Loan Contract" and the "Mortgage Contract" were entered into to perform the "Asset Transfer Contract," and the first-instance judgment correctly found all three contracts valid. First, the legal relationship between Kaili Company and Country Garden Company is essentially one of asset transfer; the "Entrusted Loan Contract" was signed to fulfill the "Asset Transfer Contract." Second, based on the terms of the "Asset Transfer Contract," "Entrusted Loan Contract," and "Mortgage Contract," the actual performance of the contracts, and the true intention of Kaili Company, the asset transfer relationship is clear and unequivocal, not a loan relationship. (2) The "Asset Transfer Contract" clearly specifies conditions for rescission; once those conditions are met, Country Garden Company has the right to rescind. The first-instance court's findings on the satisfaction of rescission conditions, the specific date of rescission, and the absence of force majeure were correct. (1) The "Asset Transfer Contract" set a deadline for completing the conditions precedent to the asset transfer. Kaili Company failed to meet those conditions by the deadline, entitling Country Garden Company to rescind. (2) The first-instance court's finding that the "Asset Transfer Contract" was rescinded on November 12, 2017, is consistent with the facts. (3) The two government policy adjustments cited by Kaili Company do not constitute force majeure. First, the notification documents regarding the shantytown renovation policy adjustment were issued in April–May 2017, and the Hainan Province "two suspensions" policy documents were issued in 2016, both predating the signing of the "Asset Transfer Contract"; the adjustments were not unforeseeable. Second, the opinion issued by the Hainan Provincial People's Government on September 28, 2017, was a reiteration of the original "two suspensions" policy, not a new policy. The relevant notification documents only imposed restrictions on financing guarantee methods, not on planning indicator adjustments. Kaili Company's evidence No. 30 submitted at first instance also demonstrates that during the performance period of the "Asset Transfer Contract," the government was still issuing policies and plans to advance the shantytown renovation project. The Hainan "two suspensions" policy involves suspending approval of new commercial housing and property-style hotel land use and suspending planning and construction approvals for new commercial housing projects, which are unrelated to planning indicator adjustments. Third, under Article 118 of the Contract Law, Kaili Company failed to promptly notify Country Garden Company after the alleged force majeure occurred; instead, it was only after Country Garden Company sent a letter demanding rescission that Kaili Company responded with a "Situation Explanation" on October 31, 2017, claiming force majeure, which clearly did not match the actual circumstances. Finally, under Article 14 of the "Asset Transfer Contract," force majeure only applies when Country Garden Company chooses to continue performance and serves to exempt Kaili Company from liability for breach. Since Country Garden Company has chosen to rescind, there is no basis for applying force majeure. (3) Given that the "Asset Transfer Contract" has been rescinded, Kaili Company must refund the earnest money and pay liquidated damages to Country Garden Company, which has the right to assert priority compensation under the "Mortgage Contract." Country Garden Company's voluntary reduction of the liquidated damages calculation standard to a 24% annual interest rate, referencing provisions on private lending, is consistent with Country Garden Company's capital investment costs and the actual interest rate levels in commercial transactions. In accordance with the relevant terms of the "Entrusted Loan Contract" and "Mortgage Contract," and the shareholders' resolution issued by Kaili Company, CCB Sanya Branch, as Country Garden Company's agent, entered into the "Mortgage Contract" with Kaili Company. Country Garden Company may directly demand that Kaili Company assume the security liability and assert the priority right to compensation over the mortgaged property. (4) Zhang Weinan, as the controlling shareholder and actual controller, fabricated debts, transferred corporate assets of Kaili Company, and seriously harmed the rights of creditor Country Garden Company, and should therefore bear joint and several liability for Kaili Company's debts. (5) This case involves only one basic legal relationship under the "Asset Transfer Contract." Country Garden Company's claims for Kaili Company's performance of its debts and for the shareholders' joint and several liability are based on closely related facts within that legal relationship, with sufficient legal basis, and are conducive to fully protecting Country Garden Company's legitimate creditor rights. The first-instance court's substantive trial of these matters collectively was procedurally proper. In conclusion, Country Garden Company requests dismissal of the appeal and affirmation of the first-instance judgment.

CCB Sanya Branch stated in its submissions that it had fully performed the "Entrusted Loan Contract," was unaware of the "Asset Transfer Contract," and only learned of its existence after the dispute arose.

Country Garden Company filed claims at first instance as follows: (1) Confirm that the "Asset Transfer Contract" is valid. (2) Confirm that the "Asset Transfer Contract" has been rescinded (the specific date of rescission to be determined by the court). (3) Order Kaili Company to immediately refund the earnest money of RMB 320,000,000 to Country Garden Company. (4) Order Kaili Company to pay liquidated damages to Country Garden Company on the basis of RMB 320,000,000 at an annual interest rate of 24%, calculated from November 3, 2017, until Kaili Company fully settles the RMB 320,000,000. (5) Order Zhang Weinan and Shengfang Company to bear joint and several liability for all debts under the above claims (3) and (4). (6) Order Zhang Weinan, Shengfang Company, and Liang Lu to bear supplementary compensation liability for the portion of corporate debts that cannot be satisfied, within the scope of the unpaid capital contribution of RMB 10,000,000 and interest. (7) Order Country Garden Company to have priority compensation from the proceeds of the auction or sale of the mortgaged property (land use rights and above-ground attachments under Real Property Certificate No. Qiong (2016) Sanya City Real Property No. XXXXXXXX) within the scope of all debts under claims (3) and (4). (8) Order Kaili Company, Zhang Weinan, Shengfang Company, and Liang Lu to bear the litigation costs of this case.

The first-instance court found the following facts: On July 15, 2017, Kaili Company passed a shareholders' resolution: (1) All shareholders of Kaili Company unanimously agreed that the company would sign the "Asset Transfer Contract" with Country Garden Company. (2) All shareholders of Kaili Company unanimously agreed to transfer all assets of the Sanya Blue Moon Bay Seaview Hotel Apartment Project (formerly the Haijing Taixin Garden Project) under the "Asset Transfer Contract" (including the target land and above-ground/underground structures). (3) All shareholders of Kaili Company unanimously agreed that shareholder Shengfang Company would pledge its 50% equity in the company, shareholder Zhang Weinan would pledge his personal 25% equity, and shareholder Liang Lu would pledge her personal 25% equity to Country Garden Company, as collateral for the loan provided by Country Garden Company to Kaili Company, securing the principal claim of RMB 130,000,000. (4) All shareholders of Kaili Company unanimously agreed to provide the company's full assets as a mortgage to Country Garden Company, as security for Kaili Company's full and proper performance of all obligations and responsibilities under the "Asset Transfer Contract," securing the principal claim of RMB 320,000,000.

2017年10月31日，凯利公司向碧桂园公司出具《情况说明》，载明按照《资产转让合同》第十四条的约定，由于三亚市政府2017年棚改项目政策调整，致使已经列入其中的网枝村棚改项目控制性规划调整未能在10月30日前完成，因而三亚蓝月湾海景酒店公寓项目虽然已经纳入网枝村棚改项目控规调整范围，但由于上述政府不可抗力原因造成规划调整无法按合同约定完成，为此，凯利公司向碧桂园公司致函说明，也希望能够就下一步合作事宜提出建议。鉴于海南明年建省30周年，中央十九大之后可能对海南国际旅游岛的发展提出更大利好政策因素，海南房地产价格总体趋高发展，土地资源更加紧缺，尤其是三亚市内海景资源会更加稀缺，而网枝村棚改项目可以提供的300亩土地就特别显得珍贵和具备更大的开发价值。网枝村已经正式列入三亚市2017年32个棚改项目，只不过是由于政府政策调整和中央十九大维稳政治要求延迟开发，不代表不能开发，只是时间问题。网枝村棚改项目，整体3.0容积率的控规指标调整在三亚市2017年32个棚改项目是最低的，而三亚蓝月湾海景酒店公寓项目作为网枝村核心地块项目，3.5容积率的控规指标调整在中国城市规划设计研究院已经完成的控规调整方案中也得到专家的认可且可以通过市规委会评审。所以，该项目控规指标的调整和网枝村棚改项目的开发都不会有根本性的改变，唯一的就是一个时间问题，中央十九大后三亚市人民政府各项工作都在加紧推进，应该近期就会有实质性进展。有鉴于此，凯利公司向碧桂园公司提出按合同约定和实际情况，顺延合同执行时间，同时为了加强合作的紧密性，能够尽快签署网枝村棚改项目框架合作协议，凯利公司在海口市江东新区参与开发的亚特兰蒂斯项目也可以委托碧桂园公司代销代建。

The court of first instance held that the issues in dispute in this case are: 1. Whether the Asset Transfer Contract has been rescinded and the specific date of rescission; 2. Whether Kelly Company should return RMB 320 million in earnest money to Country Garden Company and pay liquidated damages, as well as the standard for liquidated damages; 3. Whether Zhang Weinan and Shengfang Company should bear joint and several liability for the above debts of Kelly Company; 4. Whether Zhang Weinan, Shengfang Company, and Liang Lu should bear joint and several supplementary compensation liability within the scope of the uncontributing RMB 10 million principal and interest claimed by Country Garden Company for the above debts that Kelly Company cannot repay; 5. Whether Country Garden Company may enjoy priority right of compensation for the debts in this case against the land use right of Kelly Company under certificate No. Qiong (2016) Sanya City Real Estate Title No. XXX and the attachments above ground.

First, regarding whether the Asset Transfer Contract has been rescinded and the specific date of rescission. The Asset Transfer Contract reflected the true intentions of Country Garden Company and Kelly Company, did not violate mandatory provisions of laws or administrative regulations, and should be legal and valid. All parties in this case had no objection to the validity of the Asset Transfer Contract. Therefore, Country Garden Company's claim for confirmation of the validity of the Asset Transfer Contract was supported in accordance with the law. Article 4 of the Asset Transfer Contract stipulates: "Before applying to the competent government authority for asset appraisal, Kelly Company shall complete the following work as a condition precedent for the asset transfer under the contract: The target plot shall complete the planning adjustment and change of land use nature. Kelly Company undertakes to coordinate with the competent government authority to approve the 'Detailed Control Plan for Wangzhi Village and Surrounding Area of Hongsha Area, Sanya City, Hainan Province,' and the main planning indicators of the target plot may be adjusted as determined: Plot No. A-021, floor area ratio greater than or equal to 3.5, gross floor area (within floor area ratio) greater than or equal to 62,000 square meters, building height limit greater than or equal to 80m, building density greater than or equal to 30%, and green space ratio less than or equal to 30%. At the same time, the land use nature of the target plot may be changed from comprehensive land to Class II residential land." Article 14 of the Asset Transfer Contract stipulates: "If Kelly Company fails to complete the planning adjustment matters stipulated in Article 4 and pay the full increase and land use change fees before October 30, 2017, Country Garden Company shall have the right to unilaterally rescind the contract. However, if the above planning adjustment cannot be completed as agreed due to force majeure, Kelly Company shall not be deemed in breach, and the time for Country Garden Company or the project company to pay the loan or asset transfer loan stipulated in the contract shall be correspondingly extended." Kelly Company did not provide evidence to prove that it had completed the adjustment of planning indicators such as floor area ratio and land use nature for the subject plot under Article 4 of the Asset Transfer Contract before October 30, 2017. According to the provisions of Article 4 of the Asset Transfer Contract, Country Garden Company had the right to unilaterally rescind the contract. On November 12, 2017, Kelly Company received the Notice of Rescission of Contract and Return of Funds sent by Country Garden Company. Article 93 of the Contract Law provides: "The parties may rescind a contract upon mutual agreement. The parties may agree on the conditions under which either party may rescind the contract. When the conditions for rescission are satisfied, the person entitled to rescind may rescind the contract." Article 96 provides: "If a party claims to rescind the contract in accordance with paragraph 2 of Article 93 or Article 94 of this Law, it shall notify the other party. The contract is rescinded when the notice reaches the other party. If the other party objects, it may request the people's court or an arbitration institution to confirm the validity of the rescission." In accordance with the above provisions of the Asset Transfer Contract and the above provisions of the Contract Law, on the date when Kelly Company received the Notice of Rescission of Contract and Return of Funds sent by Country Garden Company, i.e., November 12, 2017, the legal effect of rescission of the contract had already occurred. Therefore, the Asset Transfer Contract was rescinded on November 12, 2017. Kelly Company argued that the subject project was included in the scope of shantytown renovation, the entire shantytown renovation policy of Sanya City began to be adjusted in 2016, some projects were suspended, the shantytown renovation of the subject project was suspended in October 2017 and restarted in October 2018. The adjustment of the shantytown renovation policy of the Sanya Municipal People's Government constituted force majeure, and the "two suspensions" policy issued by the People's Government of Hainan Province caused a delay in the planning adjustment progress of the target plot, making it impossible to complete the planning adjustment and change of land use nature by the contractually agreed date of October 30, 2017. In this regard, the court of first instance held that, from the time of implementation of the "two suspensions" policy of the People's Government of Hainan Province, it had already been implemented before the signing of the contract in this case, while the national shantytown policy had also been carried out since 2008 and further promoted in 2013. Even if the subject project was suspended due to policy adjustment of the Sanya Municipal People's Government in October 2017, since some other projects in Sanya had already been suspended due to government policy adjustment in 2016, Kelly Company should have foreseen the possibility that the subject project would be suspended due to the adjustment of the shantytown policy. Therefore, the adjustment of the shantytown renovation policy and the "two suspensions" policy of the People's Government of Hainan Province claimed by Kelly Company did not constitute force majeure as defined in Article 117, paragraph 2 of the Contract Law, which provides that "for the purpose of this Law, force majeure means objective circumstances that are unforeseeable, unavoidable, and insurmountable." Accordingly, Kelly Company's argument that it was not in breach and should continue to perform the Asset Transfer Contract on the ground of force majeure could not stand and was not supported in accordance with the law.

Second, regarding whether Kelly Company should return RMB 320 million in earnest money to Country Garden Company and pay liquidated damages, as well as the standard for liquidated damages. As mentioned above, the Asset Transfer Contract was rescinded on November 12, 2017. Kelly Company received the written notice of rescission from Country Garden Company on November 12, 2017, but has not returned the RMB 320 million earnest money to Country Garden Company. According to Article 17 of the Asset Transfer Contract, "If Country Garden Company rescinds the contract in accordance with the contract or legal reasons, Kelly Company shall, within three days after receiving the written notice of rescission from Country Garden Company, return the paid amounts to the designated bank account. If not returned within three days, liquidated damages shall be calculated at a rate of 5 per thousand per day on the unpaid amount to Country Garden Company or the project company." Kelly Company should have returned the RMB 320 million to Country Garden Company by November 15, 2017; if not returned, it should pay liquidated damages to Country Garden Company from November 16, 2017. The daily rate of 5 per thousand stipulated in the Asset Transfer Contract, when converted to an annual interest rate, amounts to 182.5%. In this lawsuit, Country Garden Company requests liquidated damages at an annual interest rate of 24%. Kelly Company argues that liquidated damages at 24% per annum are excessive and seeks to calculate them at the annual interest rate of 7% stipulated in the Entrusted Loan Contract. However, in actual economic activities, the cost of borrowing or the return on loans is often higher than such rate. Article 26, paragraph 1 of the Provisions of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues Concerning the Application of Law in the Trial of Private Lending Cases stipulates: "If the interest rate agreed upon between the lender and the borrower does not exceed 24% per annum, and the lender requests the borrower to pay interest at the agreed rate, the people's court shall support it." It can be seen that private lending returns within 24% per annum are lawful and protected. Accordingly, it may be determined that, except for legal relationships arising from lending and related financial business conducted by financial institutions and their branches approved and established by financial regulatory authorities, if liquidated damages for delayed refund agreed between natural persons, legal persons, and other organizations and among themselves do not exceed 24% per annum, it may not be deemed excessive. Country Garden Company is not a financial institution engaged in lending business, and its claim for liquidated damages at an annual interest rate of 24% should be supported.

Third, regarding whether Zhang Weinan and Shengfang Company should bear joint and several liability for the above debts of Kelly Company. Article 20, paragraph 3 of the Company Law provides: "If a company shareholder abuses the independent legal person status of the company and the limited liability of shareholders to evade debts and seriously damage the interests of the company's creditors, the shareholder shall bear joint and several liability for the company's debts." Country Garden Company, based on this legal provision, requests that Zhang Weinan and Shengfang Company bear joint and several liability for Kelly Company's debts in this case. Shengfang Company was once a shareholder of Kelly Company. Shengfang Company submitted the Loan Agreement, Loan Confirmation Letter, Tripartite Agreement on Entrusted Loan, Letter of Payment on Behalf, and transfer vouchers and other evidence to prove that it had a lending relationship with Kelly Company before Kelly Company transferred RMB 24,191,616 to it. This evidence formed a chain of evidence showing that Shengfang Company lent RMB 20 million to Kelly Company, and it may be determined that a lending relationship existed between Shengfang Company and Kelly Company. Therefore, Kelly Company's defense that the RMB 24,191,616 it transferred to Shengfang Company was repayment of the principal and interest on the loan it owed to Shengfang Company was established. Therefore, Country Garden Company's claim that Shengfang Company, by abusing its position as controlling shareholder, fabricated debts and transferred Kelly Company's property, thereby damaging its rights and interests, and thus requesting Shengfang Company to bear joint and several liability for Kelly Company's debts in this case, could not stand and was not supported in accordance with the law. Zhang Weinan submitted the Loan Agreement, Repayment Agreement, and the transfer voucher for Kelly Company's transfer of RMB 30 million to the Intermediate People's Court of Zhumadian City, Henan Province, but did not provide bank transfer vouchers for the payment of the RMB 20 million loan stipulated in the Loan Agreement to Kelly Company. He could not prove that Zhang Weinan had actually paid the agreed loan to Kelly Company, nor could he prove that an actual lending relationship existed between Zhang Weinan and Kelly Company. Therefore, the evidence submitted by Zhang Weinan could not prove that the RMB 29,518,384 transferred by Kelly Company to him on August 8, 2017, was repayment of a loan by Kelly Company to him. Accordingly, Country Garden Company's request, based on Article 20, paragraph 3 of the Company Law, that Zhang Weinan bear joint and several liability for Kelly Company's debts in this case had factual and legal basis and was supported in accordance with the law.

Fourth, regarding whether Zhang Weinan, Shengfang Company, and Liang Lu should bear joint and several supplementary compensation liability within the scope of the uncontributing RMB 10 million principal and interest claimed by Country Garden Company for the above debts that Kelly Company cannot repay. The Capital Verification Report (Hai Hua He Yan Zi [2015] No. 809002) issued by Hainan Huahe Certified Public Accountants on September 15, 2015, stated that the capital contribution subscribed by Shengfang Company, as a new shareholder of Kelly Company, in the amount of RMB 10 million, had been paid in full, and Shengfang Company provided the bank transfer voucher for the transfer of such RMB 10 million from Shengfang Company's account to Kelly Company's account. Therefore, it may be determined that Shengfang Company's capital increase of RMB 10 million had been actually and fully paid. Article 28, paragraph 1 of the Company Law provides: "A shareholder shall pay in full and on time the amount of capital contribution subscribed for under the articles of association. If a shareholder makes a capital contribution in currency, the shareholder shall deposit the full amount of the capital contribution in currency into the bank account opened by the limited liability company; if a shareholder makes a capital contribution in non-currency property, the shareholder shall go through the formalities for transfer of property rights in accordance with the law." Article 29 provides: "After the shareholders have subscribed for the full amount of capital contribution required by the articles of association, the representative designated by all the shareholders or the agent jointly entrusted by all shareholders shall submit the company registration application form, the articles of association, and other documents to the company registration authority to apply for establishment registration." Article 178, paragraph 1 provides: "When a limited liability company increases its registered capital, shareholders who subscribe for newly increased capital shall make capital contributions in accordance with the relevant provisions on capital contributions for the establishment of a limited liability company." According to the above legal provisions, when a shareholder makes a capital contribution in cash, depositing the corresponding cash into the company's bank account fulfills the capital contribution obligation. The business registration is a registration and filing procedure to be completed after the substantive capital contribution is made, and is not the sole basis for determining whether the shareholder's capital contribution has been made. Therefore, Country Garden Company's claim, on the ground that the business registration of Kelly Company did not record the capital contribution of Shengfang Company as having been made, requesting Zhang Weinan, Liang Lu, and Shengfang Company to bear joint and several supplementary compensation liability for Kelly Company's debts in this case within the scope of the uncontributing RMB 10 million by Shengfang Company, lacked legal basis and was not supported in accordance with the law.

Fifth, regarding the issue of whether Country Garden Company can enjoy priority right to be satisfied from the land use right with the title number Qiong (2016) Sanya Municipal Real Property Right No. XXXXXXXX and its above-ground attachments under Kaili Company's name for the debts involved in this case. The Entrusted Loan Contract and the Mortgage Contract in this case are both true expressions of the parties' intent, and do not violate mandatory provisions of laws or administrative regulations, and thus should be lawful and valid. Article 396 of the Contract Law provides: "A commission contract is a contract whereby the principal and the agent agree that the agent shall handle the principal's affairs." Article 402 provides: "Where the agent, in its own name, enters into a contract with a third party within the scope of authorization granted by the principal, and the third party, at the time of entering into the contract, is aware of the agency relationship between the agent and the principal, the contract shall directly bind the principal and the third party, unless there is conclusive evidence proving that the contract only binds the agent and the third party." Article 1 of the Entrusted Loan Contract stipulates: "Country Garden Company entrusts Sanya Branch of CCB to issue a loan of RMB 320,000,000 to Kaili Company." The Mortgage Contract stipulates: "Country Garden Company entrusts Sanya Branch of CCB, as the agent of the entrusted lender, to sign this contract with Kaili Company in the name of Sanya Branch of CCB. Either Country Garden Company or Sanya Branch of CCB may directly require Kaili Company to assume guarantee liability within the scope of guarantee as stipulated in this contract, and Kaili Company shall raise no objection." According to the provisions of the above laws and the stipulations of the contracts, Country Garden Company and Sanya Branch of CCB constitute a principal-agent relationship. The Entrusted Loan Contract and the Mortgage Contract entered into between Sanya Branch of CCB and Kaili Company directly bind Country Garden Company, and Country Garden Company holds a mortgage right over the collateral provided by Kaili Company. Kaili Company provided mortgage guarantee for the funds under the Entrusted Loan Contract by using the land use right with the title number (2016) Sanya Municipal Real Property Right No. XXXXXXXX under its name and the above-ground attachments, and has completed the mortgage registration procedures. Pursuant to Articles 180 and 187 of the Property Law, the mortgage right has been established. Article 173 of the Property Law provides: "The scope of guarantee of a security interest includes the principal claim and its interest, liquidated damages, damages for breach, costs for preserving the encumbered property and costs for enforcing the security interest. Where the parties have agreed otherwise, such agreement prevails." Article 179 provides: "To secure the performance of a debt, if the debtor or a third party does not transfer the possession of the property and mortgages such property to the creditor, and the debtor fails to pay its due debts or any circumstances as agreed by the parties for the enforcement of the mortgage occur, the creditor shall have the right to be satisfied from such property with priority." The Mortgage Contract stipulates: "Kaili Company shall establish a mortgage over the land use right with the title number Qiong (2016) Sanya Municipal Real Property Right No. XXXXXXXX under its name and the above-ground attachments, with the scope of guarantee covering the principal amount of RMB 320,000,000 under the Entrusted Loan Contract and interest, liquidated damages, compensation, other amounts payable by the debtor to the entrusted lender, and costs incurred for enforcing the claims and security rights under the Entrusted Loan Contract." Therefore, if Kaili Company fails to perform its obligation to pay the outstanding principal, interest, liquidated damages and other sums under the Entrusted Loan Contract, Country Garden Company shall have the right to be satisfied with priority from the land use right with the title number (2016) Sanya Municipal Real Property Right No. XXXXXXXX and the above-ground attachments for which the mortgage registration has been completed.

In summary, the court of first instance, in accordance with Articles 44, 96, and 107 of the Contract Law, Articles 173 and 179 of the Property Law, Article 20 of the Company Law, and Article 90 of the Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on the Application of the Civil Procedure Law of the PRC, rendered the following judgment: 1. The Asset Transfer Contract is lawful and valid; 2. The Asset Transfer Contract was rescinded on November 12, 2017; 3. Kaili Company shall, within ten days from the effective date of the judgment, refund to Country Garden Company the earnest money of RMB 320,000,000 and pay liquidated damages (the liquidated damages shall be calculated at an annual interest rate of 24% based on the principal of RMB 320,000,000 from November 16, 2017 until the date of actual full repayment); 4. Zhang Weinan shall assume joint and several liability for the debts owed by Kaili Company under item 3 of the judgment; 5. If Kaili Company fails to perform its repayment obligation under item 3 of the judgment at maturity, Country Garden Company shall have the right to be satisfied with priority from the proceeds of the discounted or auctioned/sold land use right with the title number Qiong (2016) Sanya Municipal Real Property Right No. XXXXXXXX located east of Hongsha Wangzhi Village, Jiyang District, Sanya City, and the above-ground attachments; 6. The other claims of Country Garden Company are dismissed. The case acceptance fee is RMB 3,541,800, and the preservation fee is RMB 5,000, totaling RMB 3,546,800, of which Kaili Company shall bear RMB 3,540,000 and Country Garden Company shall bear RMB 6,800.

During the second instance, Kaili Company and Zhang Weinan submitted the detailed planning modification drawings attached to the Asset Transfer Contract, to prove that the Hongsha Wangzhi Village area had been included in the 2017 shantytown renovation plan, and that the delay in planning indicators was due to government policy adjustments, which constituted force majeure and was not attributable to Kaili Company.

Country Garden Company, in its cross-examination, argued that this evidence did not constitute new evidence, had no objection to its authenticity and legality, but did not accept its purpose of proof.

Sanya Branch of CCB did not express any opinion on the cross-examination.

This Court recognizes the authenticity of this evidence, and whether it can achieve the purpose of proof will be addressed in the following issues in dispute.

In addition to confirming the facts found by the court of first instance, this Court further finds:

On February 23, 2016, the People's Government of Hainan Province issued the Notice of the People's Government of Hainan Province on Strengthening Real Estate Market Regulation and Control (Qiong Fu [2016] No. 22), part of which provides: "To all city and county people's governments, autonomous county people's governments, and units directly under the provincial government: In order to protect ecological and environmental resources, encourage housing consumption, strengthen real estate market regulation, actively reduce real estate inventory in our province, and promote the stable and healthy development of the real estate market, the relevant matters are hereby notified as follows: ... 2. Strengthen development control and reasonably control the increase of commercial housing. Strengthen the management of commercial housing land use plans and the regulation of planning approvals; for cities and counties where the commercial housing inventory digestion period exceeds the provincial average level, suspend the approval of new commercial housing (including hotel-style apartments, the same below) and property-style hotel land use (including approval for conversion of agricultural land to construction land and land expropriation, land supply approval, approval to change supplied non-commercial housing land to commercial housing land, approval for increasing the floor area ratio of commercial housing land), and suspend the planning and construction approval of new commercial housing projects. ..." On December 7, 2016, the People's Government of Hainan Province issued the Notice of the People's Government of Hainan Province on Continuing to Implement the "Two Suspensions" Policy to Further Promote the Healthy Development of the Real Estate Market (Qiong Fu [2016] No. 113). On September 28, 2017, the People's Government of Hainan Province issued the Opinions of the People's Government of Hainan Province on Further Deepening the "Two Suspensions" Policy to Promote the Stable and Healthy Development of the Real Estate Industry (Qiong Fu [2017] No. 76).

Based on the appeal grounds of the appellants and the defense opinions of the respondents, this Court considers that the issues in dispute in the second instance are: 1. The validity of the Asset Transfer Contract; 2. Whether Kaili Company constitutes a breach of contract, and whether its claim for exemption from liability due to force majeure can be established; 3. Whether the judgment of first instance correctly determined that the Asset Transfer Contract had been rescinded and calculated liquidated damages at an annual interest rate of 24%; 4. Whether Country Garden Company enjoys priority right to be satisfied from the land use right with the title number Qiong (2016) Sanya Municipal Real Property Right No. XXXXXXXX under Kaili Company's name and the above-ground attachments for the debts in this case; 5. Whether Zhang Weinan should assume joint and several liability for Kaili Company's debts; 6. Whether the court of first instance's inclusion of Zhang Weinan, Liang Lu, and Shengfang Company as defendants in this case constitutes procedural illegality.

I. Issue concerning the validity of the Asset Transfer Contract

This Court holds that paragraph 1 of Article 44 of the Contract Law provides that a contract lawfully established shall become effective upon its establishment. In this case, on July 15, 2017, Kaili Company formed a shareholders' resolution: 1. Agreed that Kaili Company would enter into the Asset Transfer Contract with Country Garden Company; 2. Agreed to transfer all assets under the Blue Moon Bay Project (including the target land and above-ground/underground buildings) under the Asset Transfer Contract... On the same day, Country Garden Company and Kaili Company entered into the Asset Transfer Contract, stipulating: Kaili Company transferred the Sanya Blue Moon Bay Seaview Hotel Apartment Project property rights to Country Garden Company; the total land area of the target plot was 16,969.08 square meters; the asset transfer price was tentatively set at RMB 700,000,000; Kaili Company would mortgage all the assets to be transferred to the project company; within 15 working days after such mortgage, Country Garden Company would pay an earnest money of RMB 320,000,000 to Kaili Company through the project company, which would be paid by Country Garden Company to Kaili Company in the form of a bank entrusted loan. It was further agreed that the earnest money would be converted into the transfer price payable by the project company to Kaili Company from the date the project company obtained new real property ownership certificates.

On August 1, 2017, Kaili Company, Country Garden Company, and Sanya Branch of CCB entered into the Entrusted Loan Contract, stipulating that Country Garden Company entrusted Sanya Branch of CCB to issue a loan of RMB 320,000,000 to Kaili Company. On August 7, 2017, Country Garden Company transferred RMB 320,000,000 from its account at Sanya Branch of CCB to Kaili Company's account at Sanya Branch of CCB.

On October 31, 2017, Kaili Company issued a Statement to Country Garden Company, stating that, in accordance with Article 14 of the Asset Transfer Contract, due to the policy adjustment of the shantytown renovation project of the Sanya Municipal People's Government in 2017, the regulatory planning adjustment for the Wangzhi Village shantytown project, which had already been included, could not be completed before October 30, and thus although the Sanya Blue Moon Bay Seaview Hotel Apartment Project had been included in the scope of the regulatory planning adjustment for the Wangzhi Village shantytown project, the planning adjustment could not be completed as stipulated in the contract due to the aforementioned government force majeure reasons. Kaili Company proposed to Country Garden Company to extend the contract execution time in accordance with the contract and the actual circumstances.

Based on the content of the above Asset Transfer Contract and the facts of its execution, it can be determined that the Asset Transfer Contract was the true expression of the intent of Kaili Company and Country Garden Company and was reached through mutual negotiation. The content of the contract does not violate the mandatory provisions of laws and administrative regulations, and should be lawful and valid. The Entrusted Loan Contract entered into among Kaili Company, Country Garden Company, and Sanya Branch of CCB was a step in the actual performance of the Asset Transfer Contract. Kaili Company's claim that the Asset Transfer Contract was in substance a loan disguised as a project asset transfer and violated mandatory provisions of laws and administrative regulations and was therefore void, lacks factual and legal basis, and this Court does not support it.

II. Issue concerning whether Kaili Company constitutes a breach of contract and whether its claim for exemption from liability due to force majeure can be established

This Court holds that, according to Article 117 of the Contract Law, force majeure refers to objective circumstances that are unforeseeable, unavoidable, and insurmountable. Article 4 of the Asset Transfer Contract stipulates: Kaili Company shall complete the following work as a prerequisite for the asset transfer under the contract: the planning adjustment and change of land use nature for the target plot. Kaili Company undertakes to coordinate with the competent government authorities for the approval of the Detailed Plan Modification for Wangzhi Village and Surrounding Areas in Hongsha Area, Sanya City, Hainan Province, so that the main planning indicators of the target plot can be adjusted as follows: plot number A-021, floor area ratio >= 3.5, building area included in floor area ratio >= 62,000 m2, height limit >= 80m, building density >= 30%, green space ratio <= 30%. The land use nature of the target plot can be changed from comprehensive land use to Class II residential land use. Article 14 stipulates: If Kaili Company fails to complete the planning adjustment as stipulated in Article 4, paragraph 1, and pay the capacity increase and nature change fees before October 30, 2017, then Country Garden Company has the right to unilaterally rescind the contract. However, if the failure to complete the aforementioned planning adjustment as stipulated in the contract is due to force majeure, Kaili Company shall not be deemed to have breached the contract, and the time for Country Garden Company or the project company to pay the loan or asset transfer loan as agreed in the contract shall be extended accordingly.

In this case, Kaili Company failed to complete the adjustment of planning indicators such as floor area ratio and land use nature for the subject land as stipulated in Article 4 of the Asset Transfer Contract before October 30, 2017. Kaili Company argued that its failure to complete the planning indicator adjustment on time was due to the "Two Suspensions" policy issued by the People's Government of Hainan Province in September 2017, which constituted force majeure, and thus it should not be deemed in breach of contract.

However, based on the facts found, on February 23, 2016, the People's Government of Hainan Province had already issued the Notice on Strengthening Real Estate Market Regulation and Control (Qiong Fu [2016] No. 22), strengthening the regulation of planning approval and management of commercial housing land use plans; for cities and counties where the commercial housing inventory digestion period exceeded the provincial average level, it suspended the approval of new commercial housing (including hotel-style apartments) and property-style hotel land use (including approval for conversion of agricultural land to construction land and land expropriation, land supply approval, approval to change supplied non-commercial housing land to commercial housing land, approval for increasing the floor area ratio of commercial housing land), and suspended the planning and construction approval of new commercial housing projects. On December 7, 2016, the People's Government of Hainan Province issued the Notice on Continuing to Implement the "Two Suspensions" Policy to Further Promote the Healthy Development of the Real Estate Market (Qiong Fu [2016] No. 113). On September 28, 2017, the People's Government of Hainan Province issued the Opinions on Further Deepening the "Two Suspensions" Policy to Promote the Stable and Healthy Development of the Real Estate Industry (Qiong Fu [2017] No. 76).

Thus, as early as February 23, 2016, the People's Government of Hainan Province had implemented the "Two Suspensions" policy. The Opinions on Further Deepening the "Two Suspensions" Policy dated September 28, 2017 (Qiong Fu [2017] No. 76) was a continuation and deepening of the Notice on Strengthening Real Estate Market Regulation and Control (Qiong Fu [2016] No. 22) dated February 23, 2016. The Asset Transfer Contract was signed on July 15, 2017. As a professional real estate investment company registered in Sanya City, Hainan Province, the "Two Suspensions" policy of the People's Government of Hainan Province was not an objective circumstance unforeseeable to Kaili Company at the time of signing the contract. Kaili Company's argument that the relevant government policy adjustment constituted force majeure and thus it should be exempted from liability lacks sufficient basis, and this Court does not support it.

III. Issue concerning whether the judgment of first instance correctly determined that the Asset Transfer Contract had been rescinded and calculated liquidated damages at an annual interest rate of 24%

Regarding whether the Asset Transfer Contract has been rescinded. Article 93 of the Contract Law provides: "The parties may rescind a contract if they reach a consensus through consultation. The parties may agree on conditions for either party to rescind the contract. When the conditions for rescission are fulfilled, the party entitled to rescind may rescind the contract." Article 96 provides: "Where a party claims to rescind the contract in accordance with paragraph 2 of Article 93 or Article 94 of this Law, it shall notify the other party. The contract is rescinded when the notice reaches the other party. If the other party objects, it may request a people's court or an arbitration institution to confirm the validity of the rescission. Where laws or administrative regulations require that the rescission of a contract be subject to approval, registration or other procedures, the provisions shall be followed." As mentioned above, Kaili Company failed to complete the agreed planning adjustment before October 30, 2017, constituting a breach of contract. According to Article 14 of the Asset Transfer Contract, which stipulates that "If Kaili Company fails to complete the planning adjustment as stipulated in Article 4, paragraph 1, and pay the capacity increase and nature change fees before October 30, 2017, then Country Garden Company has the right to unilaterally rescind the contract," Country Garden Company had the right to rescind the Asset Transfer Contract. On November 12, 2017, Kaili Company received the Demand Letter issued by Country Garden Company, which stated: Kaili Company has overdue the refund of the earnest money of RMB 320,000,000, seriously affecting Country Garden Company's funds. This letter is to inform Kaili Company again of the rescission of the contract, and requests Kaili Company to immediately and unconditionally refund the earnest money of RMB 320,000,000 and corresponding liquidated damages to Country Garden Company's account. Therefore, the judgment of first instance holding that the Asset Transfer Contract was rescinded on November 12, 2017, i.e., the date the Demand Letter reached Kaili Company, is not improper.

Regarding the issue of liquidated damages. Article 114 of the Contract Law provides: "The parties may agree that when one party breaches the contract, it shall pay a certain amount of liquidated damages to the other party based on the breach, or may agree on a method for calculating the amount of damages for losses arising from the breach. If the agreed liquidated damages are lower than the losses caused, the party may request a people's court or an arbitration institution to increase them; if the agreed liquidated damages are excessively higher than the losses caused, the party may request a people's court or an arbitration institution to appropriately reduce them. Where the parties agree on liquidated damages for delayed performance, after the breaching party pays the liquidated damages, it shall also perform its obligations." Article 29 of the Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues Concerning the Application of the Contract Law of the PRC (II) provides: "Where a party claims that the agreed liquidated damages are excessively high and requests a reduction, the people's court shall take into account the actual losses, the performance of the contract, the degree of fault of the parties, and the expected benefits, among other comprehensive factors, and make a judgment based on the principles of fairness and good faith. If the agreed liquidated damages exceed 30% of the losses caused, they may generally be deemed as 'excessively higher than the losses caused' as provided in paragraph 2 of Article 114 of the Contract Law." According to Article 17 of the Asset Transfer Contract, if Country Garden Company or the project company rescinds the contract in accordance with the contract or legal grounds, Kaili Company shall, within three days of receiving the written notice of rescission from Country Garden Company, refund all payments made by Country Garden Company or the project company to the designated bank account of Country Garden Company; if the refund is not made within three days, Kaili Company shall pay liquidated damages to Country Garden Company or the project company at a daily rate of 5 per thousand of the amount due. Kaili Company received the written notice of rescission from Country Garden Company on November 12, 2017, and should have refunded the RMB 320,000,000 to Country Garden Company by November 15, 2017. Kaili Company did not refund this amount, so it shall pay liquidated damages to Country Garden Company from November 16, 2017. The daily rate of 5 per thousand stipulated in the contract converts to an annual rate of 182.5%. Country Garden Company in its first-instance claim requested liquidated damages calculated at an annual rate of 24%. The judgment of first instance, taking into account the content of the contract, the performance circumstances, and the economic reality, referred to the interest rate standard for private lending and adjusted the liquidated damages calculation standard to an annual rate of 24%, which is not improper.

IV. Issue concerning whether Country Garden Company enjoys priority right to be satisfied from the land use right with the title number Qiong (2016) Sanya Municipal Real Property Right No. XXXXXXXX under Kaili Company's name and the above-ground attachments for the debts in this case

In this case, Article 1 of the Entrusted Loan Contract stipulates: Country Garden Company entrusted CCB Sanya Branch to grant a loan of RMB 320 million to Kaili Company. Item 3 of the "Whereas" section of the Mortgage Contract stipulates: Country Garden Company entrusted CCB Sanya Branch as the agent of Country Garden Company to sign this contract with Kaili Company in the name of CCB Sanya Branch. Item 4 of Article 8 stipulates: Either Country Garden Company or CCB Sanya Branch may directly require Kaili Company to assume the guarantee liability within the scope of guarantee under this contract, and Kaili Company shall raise no objection. Kaili Company is a party to the Entrusted Loan Contract, and the above terms are binding on it. The court of first instance ruled that Country Garden Company has a priority right to be compensated from the proceeds of discount, auction, or sale of the land use right numbered Qiong (2016) Sanya City Real Property Certificate No. ×××××××× and the above-ground attachments under Kaili Company's name for the RMB 320 million and the liquidated damages payable by Kaili Company, which has a contractual basis and is not improper.

V. Whether Zhang Weinan should bear joint and several liability for Kaili Company's debts

Article 3 of the Company Law stipulates: "A company is an enterprise legal person, has independent legal person property, and enjoys legal person property rights. A company shall bear liability for its debts with all its property. The shareholders of a limited liability company shall bear liability for the company within the amount of their subscribed capital contributions; the shareholders of a joint stock limited company shall bear liability for the company within the amount of their subscribed shares." Paragraph 3 of Article 20 stipulates: "If a company's shareholder abuses the independent legal person status of the company and the limited liability of the shareholder to evade debts and seriously damages the interests of the company's creditors, the shareholder shall bear joint and several liability for the company's debts." Independent legal person status and limited liability of shareholders are the basic principles of the Company Law. Denying the independent legal person status and requiring the shareholder who abuses the independent legal person status and limited liability to bear joint and several liability for the company's debts is an exception to limited liability. To disregard the corporate personality, it is necessary to meet the legal requirements that the shareholder has committed acts of abusing the independent legal person status and limited liability and that such acts have seriously damaged the interests of the company's creditors.

Specifically in this case, on August 7, 2017, Country Garden Company transferred RMB 320 million to Kaili Company, and on the following day, Kaili Company transferred RMB 29,518,384 to Zhang Weinan. Zhang Weinan submitted the Loan Agreement, the Debt Repayment Agreement, and a transfer voucher showing Kaili Company transferring RMB 30 million to the Intermediate People's Court of Zhumadian City, Henan Province. However, he did not submit a bank transfer voucher for the RMB 20 million loan payment to Kaili Company as agreed in the Loan Agreement, and thus failed to form a chain of evidence to prove the existence of a genuine and valid loan relationship between Zhang Weinan and Kaili Company. The judgment of the original trial found that the evidence submitted by Zhang Weinan could not prove that the RMB 29,518,384 transferred by Kaili Company to Zhang Weinan was a repayment of a loan from Kaili Company, which was not improper. However, to determine the commingling of personalities between the company and its shareholders, multiple factors need to be considered to assess whether the company has an independent will, whether the assets of the company and the shareholder are commingled and indistinguishable, and whether there are other commingling circumstances. In this case, a single transfer transaction by Kaili Company is insufficient to establish that Kaili Company and Zhang Weinan constituted commingling of personalities. Moreover, Kaili Company had set up a mortgage on the target plot under the Asset Transfer Contract for the debt in question, and Country Garden Company also failed to adduce evidence to prove that this transfer by Kaili Company seriously damaged its interests as a creditor. Therefore, the act of Kaili Company transferring RMB 29,518,384 to Zhang Weinan did not reach the level of disregarding Kaili Company's independent personality. The court of first instance's direct order for Zhang Weinan to bear joint and several liability for all of Kaili Company's debts in this case pursuant to Article 20, paragraph 3 of the Company Law was improper, and this Court hereby corrects it.

As a shareholder of Kaili Company, Zhang Weinan received a transfer of RMB 29,518,384 from Kaili Company without being able to prove a legitimate basis such as a transaction relationship or loan relationship with Kaili Company. Although this act is insufficient to negate Kaili Company's independent personality, it objectively transferred and reduced Kaili Company's assets, diminishing Kaili Company's debt-paying ability. Zhang Weinan should bear corresponding liability. The transferred amount of RMB 29,518,384 exceeded the amount of capital contribution subscribed by Zhang Weinan to Kaili Company. Based on the principle of interpreting the more serious to cover the less serious and with reference to the provisions of Article 14 of the Several Provisions of the Supreme People's Court on Application of the Company Law of the People's Republic of China (III) regarding the liability in cases of shareholders' capital contribution withdrawal, Zhang Weinan shall bear supplementary compensation liability for the portion of the RMB 320 million and the liquidated damages debts under this judgment that cannot be satisfied, within the scope of RMB 29,518,384 and the interest thereon. The interest shall be calculated on the principal of RMB 29,518,384 at the benchmark interest rate for the same period and grade issued by the People's Bank of China from August 8, 2017 to August 19, 2019, and at the loan prime rate published by the National Interbank Funding Center from August 21, 2019 onwards, calculated in stages until the date Zhang Weinan actually performs the supplementary compensation liability in full.

VI. Whether it was a procedural violation for the court of first instance to list Zhang Weinan, Liang Lu, and Shengfang Company as defendants in this case

Zhang Weinan and Liang Lu are shareholders of Kaili Company, and Shengfang Company was formerly a shareholder of Kaili Company. Country Garden Company filed suit against the three as defendants pursuant to the relevant provisions of the Company Law to assert its corresponding rights. The court of first instance listed Zhang Weinan, Liang Lu, and Shengfang Company as defendants in this case, which was procedurally lawful and not improper.

In conclusion, the Appellant's appeal grounds are partially sustained. Pursuant to Article 3 of the Company Law of the People's Republic of China and Item 2 of Article 171 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, this Court hereby renders the following judgment:

1. Affirm items 1, 2, 3, and 5 of the civil judgment (2018) Qiong Min Chu No. 6 of the Hainan High People's Court;

2. Set aside item 6 of the civil judgment (2018) Qiong Min Chu No. 6 of the Hainan High People's Court;
